speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to evaluate your systemic hypertension. Do you have any symptoms like headaches, vision changes, or nosebleeds?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is reassuring hearing he is a healthy 5-year-old with no family history. Since his blood pressure is elevated, we need to determine if this is primary hypertension or caused by a specific condition. Can you tell me exactly what his blood pressure readings have been during previous visits?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a very important finding; asymmetric blood pressure between arms in a child often suggests an underlying vascular issue. To investigate this further, I need to see the imaging results for the heart and great vessels.

REQUEST IMAGES: Echocardiogram showing the aortic arch and descending aorta.
REQUEST TEST: Upper extremity blood pressure comparison (Right arm vs Left arm).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Echocardiogram findings indicate narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation; left ventricular function is normal. Upper extremity blood pressure is 150/80 mm Hg on the right, compared to lower values in the lower extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta. The echocardiogram confirms narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery, and the significant blood pressure gradient between the upper and lower extremities is classic for this condition.
